 ALBANY, N.Y. — A high-ranking New York State Police official has been suspended without pay as state police ask the FBI to take over an investigation involving him.
 In an update on Sunday, October 25, New York State Police confirmed that Lt. Col. Jared W. Duffy has been suspended without pay.
 “The New York State Police has asked the Federal Bureau of Investigation - Albany to adopt the case involving Lieutenant Colonel Jared Duffy. Any further inquiries concerning this case should be directed to the FBI,” state police said in a statement.
 The announcement comes five days after law enforcement searched Duffy’s home in Colonie, Albany County, on October 20.
 At the time, state police confirmed that the police presence was related to an ongoing investigation and that no charges had been filed. Officials did not provide additional details about the nature of the investigation.
 On October 23, the Albany-based Times Union reported that the investigation began following a tip to the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children.
 According to the Times Union, investigators found no evidence of misconduct on Duffy’s electronic devices. The newspaper also reported that Duffy said he passed a polygraph examination.
 No criminal charges had been filed as of that report.
 Duffy serves as the Assistant Deputy Superintendent Chief of Staff for the New York State Police, overseeing projects on behalf of Superintendent James E. Barnes.
 He has served with the agency since 2002.
 State police have not publicly explained the reason for Duffy’s suspension or provided additional details about why the FBI was asked to take over the case.
 It is also unclear whether the FBI has formally accepted the request.
 CNY Central will continue to follow this developing story as more information becomes available.
